reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster because it incorporates a more structured approach to building aerobic base and introducing speed work. While Plan B includes hill repeats, it relies heavily on recovery runs, which, while important, don't directly contribute to increasing running speed. Plan A’s inclusion of a dedicated tempo run and a longer, sustained effort at threshold pace is crucial for developing the physiological adaptations needed for faster trail running. Furthermore, the inclusion of strength and mobility work is a key element often overlooked in trail running plans, contributing to injury prevention and efficiency.
